title: Zoomed all the way out: how many world cells get a pixel of their own (lab)
question: At the widest zoom-out, which of these is the game you want to be looking at?
context_md:
Your question, 2026-09-13: *"why my screen resolution can solve all of the pixels, why cannot there just be more pixels when you zoom out?"* — you were right, and this is what the answer looks like.

The renderer draws into a **fixed 512x320 buffer** and the screen magnifies that image. At the widest zoom-out the view spans 2048x1280 cells, so **fifteen of every sixteen cells never reach a pixel at all**. These three grow the buffer instead, so more of the view is carried at its own cells.

All three show the **identical patch of world at the identical size on screen** — the coarse one is magnified back up exactly as your monitor already does it. This is the **lab bed**; the outdoor skyline is a separate card, and it does not obviously agree.

The question underneath is the house style: the more cells reach the screen, the **sharper and finer** the picture, and chunky is what this game looks like.

items.label: buffer x1 (what ships today)
items.caption: one pixel per 4x4 block of world

items.label: buffer x2
items.caption: one pixel per 2x2 block of world
